provenance_summary: V1-B biological expansion wave. Microbial exopolysaccharides (EPS) produced by bacteria and fungi as bio-adsorbents for heavy metals and dyes. Rich in functional groups for pollutant binding.

mechanisms.description: EPS functional group binding: carboxyl, hydroxyl, and sulfate groups on exopolysaccharides coordinate heavy metal ions and cationic dyes

pollutant_feature.text: Heavy metal ions and cationic dyes

bio_structure.quote: protons convert phosphate, carboxyl, and sulfate groups into neutral,

interaction.text: Coordination with carboxyl, hydroxyl, sulfate groups on EPS
interaction.quote: and hydroxyl-carboxyl groups interact in coordination with heavy metal
interaction.scope_match: Keywords: sulfate, groups, hydroxyl, coordination, carboxyl

why_it_works.text: EPS can bind significant amounts of heavy metals
why_it_works.quote: Recent research outcomes on bacterial biosorption of heavy metals

causal_chain.transferable_principle: Microbial EPS carboxyl/hydroxyl/sulfate groups coordinate heavy metals and dyes

engineering_constraints.description: EPS production: microbial fermentation, yield depends on species and conditions

narrative.text: Microbial exopolysaccharides are natural biopolymers secreted by bacteria and fungi. They contain abundant functional groups (carboxyl, hydroxyl, sulfate) that can bind heavy metals and dyes. Production is scalable via fermentation.

design_translation.idea: Produce exopolysaccharides via microbial fermentation and use as bio-adsorbents for heavy metals and dyes
design_translation.design_principle: Carboxyl, hydroxyl, and sulfate groups on exopolysaccharides coordinate heavy metal ions and cationic dyes via electrostatic attraction and complexation
design_translation.implementation_example: Xanthan gum for heavy metal adsorption; Dextran-based hydrogel for dye removal
design_translation.constraints: Production cost depends on microbial fermentation efficiency; mechanical strength may need crosslinking enhancement
design_translation.failure_modes: Low mechanical strength in wet state; competitive adsorption from co-existing ions
material_realization_examples: Xanthan gum for heavy metal adsorption
design_translation.target_interaction: electrostatic attraction and complexation with metal ions and cationic dyes

knowledge_gaps: Need primary research papers with quantitative performance data
